Read the code. At bc7090d, .pre-commit-hooks.yaml declares `language: node`. package.json has a `prepack` script (`npm run build && node scripts/shrinkwrap.mjs`), so pacote must prepare the package when it is installed as a git dep. In pre-commit 4.7.0, the function pre_commit/languages/node.py:install_environment runs `npm install --allow-git=root --install-links -g git+file://<prefix>` whenever the clone has .git and package.json. Nothing in the hook config or the package avoids the git-dep preparation step.

Ran it (npm 11.20.0, Node v26.13.0, offline cache). I cloned a fresh worktree at bc7090d, then ran `npm install --offline --allow-git=root --install-links -g --prefix <scratch>/gprefix git+file://<clone>`. It failed with `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '<scratch>/gprefix/lib/node_modules/mcp-review-check/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs'`. The outer log shows `error git dep preparation failed`. The nested npm log has argv `install --force ... --include dev` with no -g, but it still writes to the global location: it shows `placeDep node_modules/mcp-review-check @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2 ...` and the ENOTEMPTY path is inside gprefix/lib/node_modules/mcp-review-check. So the nested prepare install inherits the global setting and races the outer install, as the claim says.

Severity: the root cause is npm/pacote behaviour, but the documented and shipped pre-commit integration cannot be installed with current pre-commit and npm 11, so medium fits. One correction to the claim: docs/guide/ci.md says the hook is installed "by packing the cloned repository", but pre-commit 4.x actually runs a global git+file install.

Not verified: the older pre-commit `npm pack` stdout path, npm 10, and an online install. Worktree and scratch directory removed.

Worktree at bc7090d. .pre-commit-hooks.yaml is `language: node`, and package.json:40 has `"prepack": "npm run build && node scripts/shrinkwrap.mjs"`. Tools: pre-commit 4.7.0, npm 11.20.0, Node v26.13.0, offline cache.

(1) In a scratch git repo with one committed .mcp.json, I ran `PRE_COMMIT_HOME=<scratch> npm_config_offline=true pre-commit try-repo <worktree> mcp-review-check --ref bc7090d --all-files`. It failed. pre-commit.log shows the command `node_env-default/bin/npm install --allow-git=root --install-links -g git+file://<clone>`, return code 217, and `npm error git dep preparation failed` with nested `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '<env>/lib/node_modules/mcp-review-check/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/...'`.

(2) The nested npm debug log has argv `install --force ... --include dev ...` with `placeDep ROOT mcp-review-check@1.1.0 want: file:...git-clone...` and `placeDep node_modules/mcp-review-check @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2 ...`. So the prepare child installs mcp-review-check itself into the global lib folder that the outer -g install is also writing. That is the global-config leak the finding describes.

(3) Without pre-commit, `npm install --offline --allow-git=root --install-links -g --prefix <scratch>/gp git+file://<clone@bc7090d>` failed the same way: `git dep preparation failed`, ENOTEMPTY, rc=217. It reproduced on both runs, so it is not a one-off.

So the documented `repo:` hook cannot be installed with current pre-commit/npm. docs/guide/ci.md:285 also says the hook is installed 'by packing the cloned repository', but the actual command is `npm install -g git+file://...`.

Not checked: online install, npm 10, the older pre-commit pack path, and the control run of a non-global nested install. Medium fits: a documented integration is completely broken, but the core linting is not affected and the `repo: local` fallback in the docs still works. Worktree and scratch data were removed.
